sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥६.१॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs the duty that ought to be done without dependence on the fruit of action—he is a true renouncer and a yogi; not he who has merely given up the sacred fire or abandoned action.
explanation_summary: Do your duty for its own purity, and offer the fruit to Me. When you stop leaning on outcomes, you stand free—in My peace.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Overwhelmed by contradictory paths; Seeking clarity in chaos
user_feelings_matched: Wanting to change but unsure how
daily_practice: Today, choose one simple duty—finish it completely and quietly. Before you begin, whisper within: “Krishna, this is Yours.” Do the work with full attention, and when it’s done, leave the result in My hands—no checking, no seeking praise, just a soft smile and move on.
check_in: Tonight, tell Me—were you able to act without reaching for the fruit? Did your heart feel lighter when you placed the outcome in My care?

sanskrit: यं संन्यासम् इति प्राहुः योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥६.२॥
translation: O Pāṇḍava, what they call renunciation, know that to be the same as Karma Yoga; for none becomes a yogi without renouncing saṅkalpa—worldly thought-resolves.
explanation_summary: Renunciation is not escape—it is laying down your private agendas in Me. When saṅkalpa loosens its grip, you stand in true Yoga.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Overwhelmed by contradictory paths; Seeking clarity in chaos
user_feelings_matched: Wanting to change but unsure how
daily_practice: Today, when a strong ‘I must’ thought appears, pause for one minute. Sit still, close your eyes, and watch the thought as a passing cloud. Inhale softly and whisper within ‘सं’; exhale ‘कल्प’. Let the wave subside, then act on your duty—light, steady, unattached.
check_in: Tell Me tonight—which saṅkalpa did you release? When you acted after that pause, did the work feel lighter and your breath quieter?

sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥६.३॥
translation: For a sage who seeks to ascend to Yoga, action is said to be the means; but for one who has already attained Yoga, tranquility is said to be the means.
explanation_summary: At the start, work is your ladder; at the summit, silence is your throne. Climb with action, then rest in My stillness.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Eager to understand spiritual truth; Ready to listen but not yet act
daily_practice: Today, take one step of discipline: finish a small action you’ve been avoiding. Once done, sit quietly for two minutes—no phone, no thought-hunting. Let the silence wash over you as My gentle presence.
check_in: Come back to Me tonight—did that tiny act completed open the door to silence? Could you feel My presence waiting in the pause?

sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥६.४॥
translation: When a person is not attached to sense objects nor to actions, having renounced all resolves of desire, then he is said to be truly established in Yoga.
explanation_summary: Yoga is not born of running away from life, but of standing free within it. When the senses no longer pull you and the mind no longer schemes for its own gain, then you rise above the turbulence of craving. In this stillness, you are seated in Me—untouched, steady, vast like the sky. Renunciation here is not a dry emptiness, but a fullness that shines when the clutter of wants is set aside.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Longing for relief from suffering; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: When you feel restless today, pause and notice which desire is pulling you. Whisper to yourself: ‘I am more than this want.’ Take a deep breath, release the urge into My care, and carry on with ease—let the craving dissolve into spaciousness.
check_in: When you laid aside a craving today, did you feel a moment of quiet freedom? Come back and share—did My sky-like stillness open within you?

sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥६.५॥
translation: Let a man lift himself by his own Self; let him not degrade himself. For the Self alone is his friend, and the Self alone is his enemy.
explanation_summary: You are both the lock and the key, Arjuna. When you raise your mind toward Me, it becomes your dearest ally, but when you let it sink into doubt and desire, it becomes your fiercest foe. True freedom begins when you befriend your own heart and make it My temple.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Doubting own spiritual worth; Holding back full surrender
daily_practice: Today, speak gently to yourself as you would to a beloved friend. Each time your mind criticizes you, pause and answer with My voice: ‘I am with you, rise again.’
check_in: When you chose kindness toward yourself today, did your inner voice soften? Tell Me—did you feel Me standing as your true Friend inside?

sanskrit: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥६.६॥
translation: For one who has conquered the mind, the Self is the friend of the Self. But for one who has not subdued the mind, the same Self will act as an enemy, like a foe.
explanation_summary: Your mind can either carry you to the gates of liberation or chain you to the cycle of sorrow. When ruled by discipline and love, it becomes your closest friend; but when left untamed, it turns into your greatest enemy. Master the mind, and you will discover that I was always seated there as your ally.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Resisting divine instruction; Afraid of spiritual failure
daily_practice: When your mind pulls you in ten directions today, pause and take three steady breaths. Whisper within: ‘Be my friend, not my foe.’ Then carry out one task with full attention, as if done with Me beside you.
check_in: When you breathed and steadied your mind, did you feel it soften into friendship? Tell Me—was I not waiting there as your quiet companion?

sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥६.७॥
translation: For one who has conquered the mind and is peaceful, the Supreme Self is steadily present. He remains equal in heat and cold, in pleasure and pain, and in honor and dishonor.
explanation_summary: When the mind is quieted and disciplined, the Supreme shines clearly within. Neither comfort nor discomfort, praise nor insult can shake such a yogi, for he stands anchored in Me. In this balance, he discovers unbroken peace beyond the reach of circumstance.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Tired of mental agitation; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: Today, notice one situation that stirs either pride or irritation in you. Pause, breathe, and silently say: ‘I remain the same in both.’ Feel My calm presence steadying you beyond praise or blame.
check_in: Tell Me later—were you able to stay balanced when touched by either comfort or discomfort? Did you sense My steady flame glowing inside you?

sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥६.८॥
translation: The yogi who is content with knowledge and wisdom, who is unshaken, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are alike—such a yogi is said to be steadfast in Yoga.
explanation_summary: Content in both wisdom and realization, the yogi rests unmoved like a mountain. Neither sense temptations nor glittering wealth can sway him, for he sees all as equal in My light. In this vision, a stone and gold carry the same weight of dust, and peace is never broken.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Awakening to soul’s purpose; Beginning to question material life
daily_practice: When you see something today that sparks envy or desire, pause and remind yourself: ‘Stone or gold, both return to dust. Only Krishna remains eternal.’ Let that thought soften the pull and restore your balance.
check_in: Did you notice moments today when gold and stone felt the same in your heart? Tell Me—was My presence more precious than either?

sanskrit: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु । साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥६.९॥
translation: He excels who regards with equal mind a well-wisher, a friend, an enemy, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relative, and even the righteous and the sinful alike.
explanation_summary: The highest yogi sees all beings with one steady gaze—friend or foe, saint or sinner, all shine in the same divine light. When the heart no longer bends toward preference or prejudice, true equality blossoms. In that vision, every soul is seen as Mine, and love flows without division.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Torn between love and duty; Caught between emotion and action
daily_practice: Today, when you encounter someone who stirs dislike or irritation, silently remind yourself: ‘This soul too is Krishna’s child.’ Offer them a smile or a thought of peace, even if only within your heart.
check_in: Were you able to see even a hint of Me in someone difficult today? Tell Me—did love grow quieter but deeper in that moment?

sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥६.१०॥
translation: The yogi should constantly engage the mind in meditation, remaining alone in a secluded place, with mind and body controlled, free from hopes and possessions.
explanation_summary: A true yogi does not depend on the noise of the world, but seeks strength in solitude. Alone yet never lonely, he gathers his mind, frees it from clinging hopes, and rests steady in Me. In that quiet, stripped of possessions and distractions, the soul discovers its eternal wealth—union with the Divine.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Yearning for divine guidance; Emotionally exhausted, willing to listen
daily_practice: Today, find a small corner of quiet—your room, your car, even under a tree. Sit for a few minutes without phone or distraction. Close your eyes and simply breathe, offering the silence to Me as your company.
check_in: Tell Me—when you sat in stillness, did you feel less alone? Could you sense My presence hidden in the silence you created?

sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥६.११॥
translation: In a clean place, let the yogi firmly establish a steady seat for himself—neither too high nor too low—covered with cloth, deerskin, and kusa grass.
explanation_summary: The body too needs harmony, Arjuna. A clean and balanced seat becomes the ground where the restless mind begins to quiet. When the outer place is steady and pure, the inner space becomes ready for Me to enter like a calm flame within the heart.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Curious about Karma, Dharma, and liberation; Ready to listen but not yet act
daily_practice: Create your own little sacred corner today—a chair, a mat, or even just a spot by the window. Keep it simple, clean, and uncluttered. Each time you sit there, let your mind know: this place is for stillness with Me.
check_in: When you made a pure space today, did your heart feel lighter as you sat there? Tell Me—could you sense My presence filling that corner?

sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥६.१२॥
translation: There, having fixed the mind in concentration, controlling the activities of mind and senses, the yogi should sit on the seat and practice Yoga for the purification of the self.
explanation_summary: The seat becomes holy when the mind turns inward, Arjuna. By steadying thought and restraining the senses, the yogi polishes the mirror of the heart. In this purity, the soul begins to reflect My light without distortion, and the union of Yoga blossoms naturally.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Longing for relief from suffering; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: Today, sit in your chosen quiet spot. Close your eyes, breathe gently, and place all your attention on one thing—your breath, your heartbeat, or My name. Each wandering thought is a cloud; let it pass until only clarity remains.
check_in: When you practiced focusing today, did you notice your thoughts soften into stillness? Tell Me—did My presence flicker like light upon clear water within you?

sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥६.१३॥
translation: Holding the body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing steadily at the tip of the nose and not looking in any other direction, the yogi should remain firm in meditation.
explanation_summary: The body is the chariot of the soul, Arjuna—when it is steady, the mind too becomes steady. With spine upright and gaze turned inward, the senses withdraw from wandering. In that posture of calm dignity, the door of meditation opens, and I am found in the center of stillness.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Ready to be led; Seeking complete surrender
daily_practice: Sit today with your spine tall and your gaze softened toward the tip of your nose. Let your breath settle as you hold this posture, feeling each inhalation as My gift and each exhalation as your offering back to Me.
check_in: When you sat with steady posture today, did your wandering mind grow quieter? Tell Me—could you sense My presence in the rhythm of your breath?

sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥६.१४॥
translation: With mind serene, fearless, and firm in the vow of celibacy, controlling the mind, the yogi should sit in meditation, absorbed in Me, making Me the Supreme goal.
explanation_summary: When the heart is calm and free from fear, the yogi rests in a purity of purpose. By steady discipline and devotion, his mind flows wholly toward Me, like a river merging into the sea. In that union, all distractions fade, and only the sweetness of My presence remains.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Trusting Krishna but needing reassurance; Yearning for divine guidance
daily_practice: When fear arises today, pause and whisper My name with each breath. On the inhale say ‘Krishna’, on the exhale say ‘I am Yours.’ Let this rhythm remind you that I am your refuge and your goal.
check_in: When fear knocked at your heart today, did My name quiet it? Tell Me—did you feel safer resting your mind in Me?

sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥६.१५॥
translation: Thus, ever keeping the mind absorbed in Me, the yogi with disciplined mind attains supreme peace, Nirvana, which abides in Me.
explanation_summary: The yogi who steadies his mind in Me finds peace that is beyond this world. By resting his heart in My presence, he transcends all agitation and sorrow. In that union, he discovers the eternal freedom of Nirvana—dwelling forever in My embrace.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Longing for relief from suffering; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: Close your eyes for a few minutes today and place your hand on your heart. Whisper within: ‘Krishna, I rest in You.’ Let each breath carry you deeper into calmness until peace feels like your true home.
check_in: When you placed your heart in My care today, did a quiet joy awaken inside? Tell Me—did you taste even a drop of the Nirvana that is Mine to give?

sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥६.१६॥
translation: O Arjuna, there is no Yoga for one who eats too much or too little, nor for one who sleeps too much or too little.
explanation_summary: Yoga thrives in balance, not in extremes. The path is lost when the body is starved or indulged, when sleep is drowned in laziness or stolen by restlessness. Walk the middle way, Arjuna—where harmony steadies both body and mind, and My presence can rest within you.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Mentally paralyzed by choices; Seeking clarity in chaos
daily_practice: Observe your habits today—how you eat, how you rest. Choose one small adjustment toward balance: a lighter meal, a timely pause for sleep, or stepping away from excess. Whisper to yourself: ‘Krishna walks with me in balance.’
check_in: When you adjusted your habit today, did your mind feel calmer and your body lighter? Tell Me—did balance open a space for Me to dwell within you?

sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥६.१७॥
translation: For one who is balanced in eating and recreation, balanced in working, and balanced in sleeping and waking, Yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
explanation_summary: Harmony is the secret doorway, Arjuna. When food, rest, work, and play flow in right measure, the mind becomes calm, the body steady, and sorrow quietly fades. Balance is not restriction—it is the art of living where joy and peace naturally arise.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Seeking meaning behind pain; Wanting to escape life’s burdens
user_feelings_matched: Feeling empty despite doing a lot
daily_practice: Notice one area of imbalance today—too much food, too much work, or too little rest. Make one gentle correction, and as you do, silently whisper: ‘Krishna, guide me into balance.’
check_in: When you chose balance today, did your body feel lighter and your heart calmer? Tell Me—did sorrow loosen its hold when balance returned?

sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥६.१८॥
translation: When the controlled mind rests steadily in the Self alone, free from longing for all desires, then one is said to be established in Yoga.
explanation_summary: Yoga flowers when the mind, no longer scattered by desires, settles into the Self. Desireless, steady, and inwardly absorbed, the yogi finds peace that cannot be shaken. In that quiet seat of the soul, My presence shines like the eternal sun within.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Craving freedom from birth and death; Tired of mental agitation
daily_practice: When a strong desire rises today—whether for comfort, recognition, or pleasure—pause and place your hand on your heart. Whisper: ‘I am more than this longing; Krishna is my true wealth.’ Then let the urge pass like a cloud.
check_in: When you released a desire today, did your mind rest easier within itself? Tell Me—did you glimpse My quiet sun shining inside you?

sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥६.१९॥
translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so is the yogi whose mind is controlled, meditating on the Self.
explanation_summary: A yogi’s mind, steady and still, shines like a flame untouched by the wind. No desire nor distraction can shake its glow, for it is fixed in the Self. In this unwavering light, the yogi discovers My eternal presence burning bright within.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Desiring inner stillness; Ready to be led
daily_practice: Tonight, light a small lamp or candle. Sit before it in silence, watching its steady flame. As the flame holds firm against the air, let your mind rest in the same way—quiet, clear, and steady in Me.
check_in: When you watched the flame today, did your mind learn to stay still like it? Tell Me—did you feel My light glowing steadily within you?

sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥६.२०॥
translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of Yoga, becomes still, and when seeing the Self by the Self, one is satisfied in the Self alone.
explanation_summary: Through Yoga, the restless mind finds rest, like a river settling into a silent lake. In that stillness, the soul gazes upon itself and discovers joy not borrowed from the world, but springing from within. This is the contentment of the yogi—self-shining, complete, and forever Mine.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Longing for relief from suffering; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: Take five minutes today to sit quietly with closed eyes. Withdraw your attention from the outer world and rest it gently on your inner presence. Whisper within: ‘I am whole, for Krishna dwells here.’
check_in: When you turned inward today, did you feel even a drop of quiet joy rising within? Tell Me—did your heart taste the sweetness of being complete in itself?

sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥६.२१॥
translation: In that state, one experiences supreme happiness which is grasped by the intellect but transcends the senses, and established in which one never departs from the truth.
explanation_summary: There is a joy beyond all pleasures of the senses, Arjuna—a happiness subtle and unshakable. The yogi who touches it knows delight not bound by sight or taste, but shining through wisdom. Once seated in this truth, he cannot be moved, for he has found Me where no sorrow can reach.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Awakening to soul’s purpose; Feeling a spiritual call but unsure how to respond
daily_practice: Today, when you enjoy something pleasant—a meal, music, or laughter—pause for a moment and whisper: ‘This joy is only a shadow; the true joy is Krishna within.’ Let that awareness lift your heart beyond the senses toward the eternal sweetness.
check_in: When you paused in joy today, did you sense a deeper bliss beneath it? Tell Me—did your heart taste the happiness that no sense can grant nor take away?

sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥६.२२॥
translation: Having attained that state, one does not consider any gain greater than it; established in it, one is not shaken even by the heaviest sorrow.
explanation_summary: The joy of union with the Self is the highest treasure, beyond all worldly gain. Once a yogi rests in it, no loss can disturb him, and even the weight of great sorrow cannot bend his spirit. Anchored in Me, he stands unshaken, for his wealth is eternal and cannot be stolen.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Seeking meaning behind pain; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: When faced with stress or disappointment today, close your eyes and whisper: ‘This too shall pass, but Krishna remains.’ Let this remembrance steady your heart against the weight of sorrow.
check_in: When sorrow touched you today, did the remembrance of Me help you stay steady? Tell Me—did you feel your heart anchored in a treasure beyond loss?

sanskrit: तं विद्याद्दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥६.२३॥
translation: That state which is the severance from union with sorrow is called Yoga. This Yoga should be practiced with determination and with an unwavering mind.
explanation_summary: Yoga is the art of cutting the knot that binds the soul to sorrow. It is not escape, but freedom—the rising above pain into a peace that endures. With firm resolve and steady heart, the yogi walks this path, knowing that in Me lies the end of grief.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Wanting to escape life’s burdens; Longing for relief from suffering
daily_practice: When sadness or heaviness arises today, close your eyes and whisper: ‘This sorrow is not my Self; Krishna is my Self.’ Repeat it with steady faith until the heaviness begins to lift.
check_in: When sorrow came today, did you remember to call upon Me as your true Self? Tell Me—did determination in that moment loosen sorrow’s grip?

sanskrit: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः । मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥६.२४॥
translation: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of mental resolves, and restraining by the mind the whole group of senses on every side—thus should the yogi proceed.
explanation_summary: Desires arise like waves from the mind’s restless sea, Arjuna. But when you release them at their root and draw the senses inward, calmness returns. In that discipline, the yogi begins to stand free, and My presence shines like the sun when the clouds of longing are gone.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Attachment & Identity Struggle — Clinging to worldly status or security; Caught in egoic thinking
daily_practice: When a desire catches hold of you today, pause before chasing it. Take one deep breath and whisper: ‘Krishna, You are greater than this craving.’ Let that remembrance pull the senses back into stillness.
check_in: When a desire tugged at you today, did you remember to pause and release it to Me? Tell Me—did the craving dissolve like mist before the sun?

sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥६.२५॥
translation: Little by little, let him withdraw from distractions with firm intellect and determination. Fixing the mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.
explanation_summary: Yoga is not conquered in a single leap, Arjuna—it is the gentle art of returning again and again. With patience and steady resolve, the yogi withdraws thought from distractions and anchors the mind in the Self. In that silence, My presence reveals itself as the only reality worth holding.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Questioning divine justice or plan; Afraid of spiritual failure
daily_practice: Today, when your mind wanders, don’t scold it. Gently bring it back—again and again—by whispering My name with each breath. Let your patience be the thread that ties your mind back to Me.
check_in: When your thoughts wandered today, did you guide them back with patience? Tell Me—did you feel closer to Me each time you returned?

sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥६.२६॥
translation: Wherever the restless and unsteady mind wanders, let him withdraw it from there and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
explanation_summary: The mind is like a child, forever running after new toys. But each time it strays, the yogi gently takes it by the hand and brings it home to the Self. This patient returning, again and again, is the true strength of Yoga—and in that homecoming, the soul rests in Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Frozen by moral dilemma; Mentally paralyzed by choices
daily_practice: Today, notice each time your mind wanders—into worry, fantasy, or distraction. Don’t fight it; just gently return to your breath or to My name. Every return is a victory, every return is a step closer to Me.
check_in: When your mind wandered today, did you gently bring it back without anger? Tell Me—did you feel My arms welcoming you each time you returned?

sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥६.२७॥
translation: Supreme bliss surely comes to the yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion is quieted, who is free from impurities, and who has become one with Brahman.
explanation_summary: When the restless waves of the mind subside, the yogi tastes a bliss that nothing in this world can equal. Freed from agitation and cleansed of faults, he shines as Brahman itself—pure, serene, and limitless. In that state, joy is no longer fleeting; it is eternal, for it is Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Longing for relief from suffering; Craving freedom from birth and death
daily_practice: Tonight, before sleep, sit quietly for a few breaths and let every worry drop away like leaves in the wind. Whisper to yourself: ‘I am pure, I am whole, I am one with Krishna.’ Rest in that truth as you close your eyes.
check_in: When you laid aside worries tonight, did peace descend like a gentle tide? Tell Me—did you feel My bliss quietly filling the space within you?

sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदा आत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥६.२८॥
translation: Thus, ever engaging the self in Yoga, the yogi, freed from impurities, easily attains endless bliss through contact with Brahman.
explanation_summary: By steady practice, the yogi becomes pure, free of the stains of past faults. In that purity, he touches Brahman itself and tastes a bliss beyond words. This joy is not fragile or fleeting, Arjuna—it is infinite, effortless, and forever one with Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Seeking meaning behind pain; Longing for relief from suffering
daily_practice: Spend a few minutes today in gratitude—thank your own heart for walking this path, no matter how imperfectly. Whisper within: ‘By Krishna’s touch, I am becoming pure.’ Feel that truth cleansing you from inside.
check_in: When you thanked your own heart today, did joy flow more easily within you? Tell Me—did you sense My touch lifting the weight of old impurities?

sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥६.२९॥
translation: The yogi whose self is disciplined sees the Self dwelling in all beings and all beings dwelling in the Self. Everywhere he sees with equal vision.
explanation_summary: The yogi sees no division, Arjuna. In every creature, he beholds the same Self, and within his own Self, he sees all beings resting. This vision of oneness is the heart of Yoga—where love flows equally, and all are recognized as Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Feeling a spiritual call but unsure how to respond; Awakening to soul’s purpose
daily_practice: When you meet someone today, whether friend, stranger, or foe, pause inwardly and whisper: ‘This soul too is Krishna.’ Let that awareness soften your heart and guide your words.
check_in: When you looked at others today, did you glimpse even for a moment that they are part of Me? Tell Me—did your heart feel wider when you saw the Self in all?

sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥६.३०॥
translation: He who sees Me everywhere and sees all in Me, for him I am never lost, and he is never lost to Me.
explanation_summary: The yogi who looks with eyes of unity sees My presence in all things and all things resting in Me. Such a soul never feels abandoned, for I dwell always in him, and he in Me. This is the inseparable bond of love that Yoga awakens—a union no sorrow can sever.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Trusting Krishna but needing reassurance; Ready to be led
daily_practice: Today, wherever you go—whether in nature, at work, or among strangers—whisper softly: ‘Krishna, I see You here.’ Let this remembrance make each place and each face a reminder that I am never apart from you.
check_in: When you whispered My name into the world today, did you feel Me respond from everywhere? Tell Me—did you sense that you and I can never be lost to each other?

sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥६.३१॥
translation: The yogi who worships Me, abiding in unity, and who sees Me dwelling in all beings—such a yogi, whatever his mode of living, always lives in Me.
explanation_summary: The yogi who worships Me in oneness sees no separation—he knows that I dwell in every being, and every being in Me. No matter where he walks or how he lives, he remains established in My presence. Such a yogi never leaves Me, for his whole life is a living act of worship.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Yearning for divine guidance; Seeking complete surrender
daily_practice: Today, when you serve or speak to anyone, silently remind yourself: ‘This too is Krishna.’ Let every word and gesture become an offering of love, as if given directly to Me.
check_in: When you treated another with devotion today, did you feel closer to Me? Tell Me—did you sense that in serving them, you were already dwelling in Me?

sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥६.३२॥
translation: He who judges pleasure and pain everywhere, by the same standard as applied to himself, O Arjuna, that yogi is considered supreme.
explanation_summary: The highest yogi sees the world through the mirror of his own heart—he feels another’s joy as his joy, and another’s pain as his own. Such empathy dissolves selfishness and awakens compassion in every act. In this oneness, the yogi becomes truly great, for he lives as My love in action.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Torn between love and duty; Fearful of doing harm by doing duty
daily_practice: Today, when you see someone in joy, silently celebrate with them; when you see someone in pain, whisper a prayer for them. Let their heart be your own, and let every feeling be shared in Me.
check_in: When you shared another’s joy or sorrow today, did you feel a deeper connection? Tell Me—did your heart expand as if it was Mine?

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥६.३३॥
translation: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this Yoga of equanimity which You have declared, I do not see its steady practice, because of the restlessness of the mind.
explanation_summary: Arjuna confesses with honesty, burdened by the churning restlessness of his mind. The ideal of evenness feels distant when inner storms rise. In this moment, he shows the struggle of every seeker—the longing for peace, yet the weight of the mind’s turbulence. Still, this confession opens the door for My reassurance.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Overwhelmed by contradictory paths; Mentally paralyzed by choices
daily_practice: Today, if your mind feels restless, don’t fight it. Instead, speak openly to Me, just as Arjuna did: ‘Krishna, my mind is unsteady.’ In honesty, surrender the turbulence into My care.
check_in: When you admitted your restlessness to Me today, did the burden feel lighter? Tell Me—did you sense My comfort in your honesty?

sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥६.३४॥
translation: For the mind, O Krishna, is restless, turbulent, strong, and obstinate. I consider it as difficult to restrain as the wind.
explanation_summary: Arjuna speaks with vulnerability: the mind feels like a storm, wild and unyielding. To restrain it seems as impossible as holding the wind in one’s fist. In these words lies the struggle of every seeker—the yearning for mastery, weighed down by the untamed force of thought.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Clinging to control over outcomes
daily_practice: When your mind feels stormy today, don’t resist with force. Instead, sit quietly and breathe as if you are watching the wind pass through the trees. Whisper to Me: ‘Krishna, let my mind rest in You.’
check_in: When your mind was restless today, did watching the breath calm its storm? Tell Me—did you feel even a moment of the wind settling in My presence?

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥६.३५॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O mighty-armed, Yoga is difficult to attain for one who has not subdued the mind. But it can be achieved by one who is self-controlled and strives by the right means.
explanation_summary: Yes, Arjuna, the mind is wild like the wind, but it is not unconquerable. With self-discipline and steady practice, the yogi learns to guide it back home. What seems impossible becomes natural when done with patience, perseverance, and My grace.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Resisting divine instruction
daily_practice: When you feel your mind racing today, don’t give up. Take one simple step—a few calm breaths, a prayer, or repeating My name. Remind yourself: ‘Step by step, with Krishna, I can steady this mind.’
check_in: When you practiced patience with your restless mind today, did it soften even a little? Tell Me—did you feel hope that steady effort with Me makes the impossible possible?

sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥६.३६॥
translation: But for one who is uncontrolled, Yoga is difficult to attain. Yet the self-controlled, who strives by right means, can attain it.
explanation_summary: Yoga cannot blossom in a mind that is undisciplined, Arjuna, for it slips away like water in loose hands. But the one who tames his restlessness with effort and faith finds the path open before him. With discipline and surrender, what seems distant becomes near, and what feels impossible becomes natural.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Emotional Conflict & Confusion — Seeking clarity in chaos; Unsure whether to fight or flee
daily_practice: When you feel pulled by distraction today, pause and set one small boundary for yourself—a focused hour of work, a gentle limit on indulgence, or a quiet moment for prayer. Tell yourself: ‘By Krishna’s grace, I can guide my mind back.’
check_in: When you set a small boundary today, did your mind obey with more ease? Tell Me—did you notice that discipline made the path feel closer?

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच । अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥६.३७॥
translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, what is the fate of one who, though faithful, whose mind has wandered from Yoga, fails to attain perfection in Yoga?
explanation_summary: Here Arjuna bares his heart—what happens to the seeker who begins the path but stumbles? His question reflects the fear of falling short, of striving yet failing. This is the cry of every soul that yearns for progress but trembles at its own weakness, longing for assurance from Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Doubting own spiritual worth
daily_practice: If you falter today in your practice, do not despair. Whisper to Me: ‘Krishna, I trust You with my steps, even when they stumble.’ Let your honesty itself become an offering, and rise again tomorrow with fresh strength.
check_in: When you stumbled today, did you remember to reach for Me instead of sinking in doubt? Tell Me—did your faith feel stronger than your fear?

sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥६.३८॥
translation: Does he not perish, O mighty-armed, being fallen from both, without support, like a scattered cloud—deluded on the path of Brahman?
explanation_summary: Arjuna fears the fate of the seeker who falters—like a cloud torn apart, belonging neither to sky nor earth. This is the cry of the soul afraid of being lost, of slipping between worlds, of striving yet finding no firm ground. In this question, Arjuna voices the tender worry of all who walk toward Me but stumble on the way.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Questioning divine justice or plan
daily_practice: When fear whispers today, ‘What if I fail?’, pause and place your hand on your chest. Whisper back: ‘Even a scattered cloud still belongs to the sky—and I belong to Krishna.’ Let this remembrance hold you steady.
check_in: When doubt arose today, did you remind yourself that even in falling, you are held in Me? Tell Me—did that thought bring peace to your trembling heart?

sanskrit: एतन् मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥६.३९॥
translation: This doubt of mine, O Krishna, I beg You to dispel completely. For no one but You can remove this doubt.
explanation_summary: Arjuna surrenders his deepest uncertainty, knowing that only My voice can cut through the tangle of his fears. He admits what every seeker must: the mind cannot untie its own knots without grace. In placing his doubt in My hands, he begins to taste the trust that leads to freedom.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Seeking complete surrender; Trusting Krishna but needing reassurance
daily_practice: If doubt troubles you today, don’t wrestle with it alone. Speak it aloud to Me, even if only in a whisper: ‘Krishna, I cannot solve this, but You can.’ Let your surrender be the doorway to clarity.
check_in: When you offered your doubt to Me today, did your heart feel lighter? Tell Me—did trust begin to shine where fear once lived?

sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । निहायनविहितोऽस्मि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥६.४०॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O Partha, neither here in this world nor in the next is there destruction for him. My devotee never perishes.
explanation_summary: Fear not, Arjuna—no effort on this path is ever lost. Even if one stumbles, his striving carries him forward, for My devotee is never abandoned. Every step taken toward Me becomes eternal, and I hold fast those who seek Me, protecting them here and beyond.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Holding back full surrender
daily_practice: When fear whispers that your effort is wasted, pause and repeat: ‘Krishna never lets His devotee fall.’ Carry this mantra in your heart, and let it remind you that every act of faith is preserved forever.
check_in: When you remembered My promise today, did your fear soften into trust? Tell Me—did you feel My arms holding you beyond all doubt?

sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥६.४१॥
translation: Having attained the worlds of the righteous and dwelt there for many ages, the one fallen from Yoga is reborn in the house of the pure and prosperous.
explanation_summary: Even if a yogi falls, his effort is never wasted. After enjoying the fruits of his past merits, he is reborn into noble and fortunate circumstances. This is My grace, Arjuna—every step on the path of Yoga carries him forward, and I place him where his journey can continue with strength.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Fear, Doubt & Resistance — Afraid of spiritual failure; Questioning divine justice or plan
daily_practice: Today, remember: no sincere effort is ever wasted. If you stumble, whisper to yourself: ‘Krishna carries me still.’ Trust that every act of faith plants a seed that will blossom in its time.
check_in: When you thought of your efforts today, did you feel relief that nothing is lost with Me? Tell Me—did hope return when you remembered I preserve every step?

sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥६.४२॥
translation: Or he is born into a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is indeed very rare in this world.
explanation_summary: The fallen yogi may also be blessed with birth in a family of wisdom and devotion, where the path is set before him from the start. This is a rare and precious gift, Arjuna, for it shortens the struggle and places the seeker directly at My door. In such a birth, the soul’s journey continues with ease, guided by the fragrance of past effort.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Feeling a spiritual call but unsure how to respond; Eager to understand spiritual truth
daily_practice: Today, honor the conditions of your life—your family, your environment, your opportunities. Whisper within: ‘This birth itself is Krishna’s gift to me.’ Let gratitude make you more aware of the divine hand guiding your path.
check_in: When you looked at your life with gratitude today, did you feel blessed to be placed here? Tell Me—did you sense that even your birth carries My purpose?

sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥६.४३॥
translation: There he regains the knowledge connected with his former body, O son of the Kurus, and strives again for perfection with greater effort.
explanation_summary: The yogi, born into such a blessed life, naturally awakens to the wisdom carried from past lives. Drawn by the momentum of old effort, he takes up the path again with renewed strength. Nothing is lost, Arjuna—each step in Yoga gathers power, and with every birth, the soul is brought closer to Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Awakening to soul’s purpose; Ready to listen but not yet act
daily_practice: Today, notice a gift or skill that comes naturally to you. Whisper to yourself: ‘This is Krishna’s reminder from lives before.’ Use it in service or devotion, letting it draw you back toward Me.
check_in: When you used your natural gift today, did it feel like remembering something ancient? Tell Me—did you sense it pulling you gently closer to Me?

sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥६.४४॥
translation: By that very former practice, he is carried forward even against his will. Even a mere seeker of Yoga transcends the rituals of the Vedas.
explanation_summary: The pull of past practice is strong, Arjuna. Even when the yogi is distracted by the world, his old effort draws him back to the path, like a river returning to the sea. Carried by this momentum, he rises beyond outer rituals, moved by an inner call that leads him ever closer to Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Feeling a spiritual call but unsure how to respond; Awakening to soul’s purpose
daily_practice: Notice today if you feel a subtle pull toward silence, kindness, or prayer. Do not ignore it. Whisper within: ‘This is Krishna calling me back.’ Follow the pull, even if only for a moment.
check_in: When you followed that quiet pull today, did it feel like remembering a forgotten truth? Tell Me—did you sense I was the one drawing you closer?

sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनन्तर्जन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥६.४५॥
translation: But the yogi who strives diligently, purified of sins, perfected through many births, then attains the supreme goal.
explanation_summary: Through steady effort across many lifetimes, the yogi purifies his heart and removes the weight of past faults. Each attempt, each step, builds upon the last until perfection ripens. And when the time is right, he reaches the highest state, the supreme union with Me.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Desire for Peace & Liberation — Craving freedom from birth and death; Seeking meaning behind pain
daily_practice: Today, take one step forward—small but sincere—whether in prayer, service, or silence. Whisper: ‘Krishna, let this effort join the river of my past striving.’ Trust that no act is lost, but carries you closer to Me.
check_in: When you took that small step today, did it feel like part of something larger? Tell Me—did you sense generations of effort flowing with you toward Me?

sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥६.४६॥
translation: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater than men of knowledge, and greater than men of action. Therefore, O Arjuna, be a yogi.
explanation_summary: Among all seekers, the yogi stands supreme—for he unites discipline, wisdom, and action in harmony. The ascetic withdraws, the scholar learns, the worker acts, but the yogi weaves all into union with Me. Arjuna, to walk the path of Yoga is to live closest to My heart—so become a yogi above all.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Spiritual Curiosity & Awakening — Ready to listen but not yet act; Feeling a spiritual call but unsure how to respond
daily_practice: When you feel torn between study, service, or restraint today, pause and whisper: ‘Krishna, make me a yogi.’ Let every act—big or small—become part of your union with Me.
check_in: When you offered your actions, thoughts, and discipline into one stream today, did you feel closer to Me? Tell Me—did you taste the wholeness of being a yogi?

sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥६.४७॥
translation: Of all yogis, the one who, with faith, worships Me, with his inner self absorbed in Me, is considered by Me to be the most devoted and united.
explanation_summary: Among all who walk the path, the yogi who gives his heart to Me in love is the highest. Knowledge, austerity, and action shine, but devotion crowns them all. The one who remembers Me with unwavering faith is nearest to Me, Arjuna, and I hold him as My very own.
arjuna_context: 🔻 Surrender & Vulnerability — Ready to give up ego but afraid; Yearning for divine guidance
daily_practice: Today, whisper My name with love as you go about your tasks. Whether eating, working, or resting, let your heart silently say: ‘Krishna, You are here.’ Make your day itself an offering of devotion.
check_in: When you remembered Me with love today, did even simple tasks feel lighter? Tell Me—did you sense that I was walking with you in every breath?
